core: do not hash header if header is still changing

**Description**

In the block-building code (triggered by `miner` package `commitTransaction`, which is used by engine-API) it runs this code-path where every time a transaction is applied, it takes the template block-header and re-encodes and hashes it.
This same function is also used by the op-program version of the engine-API.

This is inefficient in the same way in upstream L1 geth block-building code too.

One way to temporay-fix it, is to not compute the block-hash, when the state-root is still not set. A zero state-root implies that the block-building is not done.

This is a temporary fix. Ideally we improve the geth block-building API, so it's not running into this thing to begin with. Constructing receipts on the way is one thing, but trying to hydrate the metadata before the block is even finished is just bad.

This PR is a draft to help track this optimization until upstream block-building is improved.

op-node: Skip L1 genesis hash check if block is not available from the L1

**Description**

Skip L1 genesis hash check if block is not available from the L1.

With block and receipt data being pruned on a rolling basis from L1 nodes having a requirement that a very old, fixed block is present just to check a config that is often built into op-node itself seems unreasonable.

Without this, using Nethermind as the L1 with `--history-pruning=Rolling` (unclear if this is the default now) op-node fails to start with:
```
failed to init L1: failed to validate the L1 config: failed to get L1 genesis blockhash: failed to fetch header by num 17422590: not found
```

Compose TimelockGuard and LivenessModule2 into a single contract

**Description**

`TimelockGuard` and `LivenessModule2` are inherited into a single contract. The primary purpose of which is to avoid the need to deploy and manage two different contracts.

Also makes the parent contracts abstract in order to prevent deploying
them individually.


Since their functionality is otherwise distinct, the child contract contains none of its own logic. The benefit of this approach is that it ensures the logic is available
in both contracts, while ensuring that their state and logic are kept
separate thus reducing the complexity and review effort.

Tests are kept separate for the same reason.

op-sync-tester: Retry block fetching when processing newPayload

<!--
Contributions welcome! See https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/.github/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

**Description**

`TestSyncTesterELSync` flaked because when sync tester receives `engine_newPayload`, it tries to validate the newpayload, comparing the payload from the payload generated by blockInfo fetched from the read only EL.

The race window happens when sync tester is processing the payload very near the unsafe chain tip. Read Only EL may temporally respond with `ethereum.NotFound` error. The maximum race window will be a single block time(2 second). 

So when the first try of fetching block failed with `ethereum.NotFound` error, we now gracefully retry to fetch the block once again after waiting single block time(2 second).

Note that validator may receive sequencer signed unsafe payload, before the sequencer controlled EL be queried that unsafe payload. 

Reenabling the sync test that was skipped.

**Tests**

All existing tests are passing

**Metadata**

- Fixes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/17615

# Add AI Contract Test Maintenance System v0.1.0

## Overview

This PR introduces the **AI Contract Test Maintenance System**, an automated toolchain designed to continuously reduce technical debt in contract tests within the `contracts-bedrock` monorepo. The system integrates with an AI coding agent to generate pull requests that improve test quality and coverage.

## What's in this PR (v0.1.0)

### Test Ranking System
- **Test selection** based on staleness metrics between test files and their corresponding source contracts
- **Two-branch scoring algorithm** that prioritizes tests whose contracts have diverged ahead, then falls back to test age
- **Git-based analysis** using commit timestamps to calculate staleness and priority scores.

## Sample Output

The system generates a ranked JSON file with entries like:

```json
{
  "generated_at": "2025-09-22T...",
  "entries": [
    {
      "test_path": "test/L1/ProtocolVersions.t.sol",
      "contract_path": "src/L1/ProtocolVersions.sol", 
      "staleness_days": -98.21,
      "score": 135.84
    }
  ]
}
```

Higher scores indicate higher priority for maintenance attention.

## Documentation

- **Operational Runbook** (`docs/runbook.md`) - System overview, usage, and troubleshooting

Tighten directory permissions for file-backed KV store

### Description
- **What**: Use `0700` instead of `0777` when auto-creating the KV store directory in `op-program/host/kvstore/file.go`.
- **Why**: Principle of least privilege; avoids world-writable or world-readable dirs depending on `umask`. Security hardening with no functional change for single-process usage.
- **Change**: `os.MkdirAll(dir, 0777)` → `os.MkdirAll(dir, 0700)`.
- **Impact**: Should be transparent for typical deployments. If other users/processes previously relied on wider permissions, they may need explicit access.

op-dispute-mon: Consider node invalid if it has not processed L1 past the game head

**Description**

Update op-dispute-mon so that it checks the rollup node sync status and considers it invalid if `CurrentL1` is not above the game's L1 head block number. This ensures that the node's safe head correctly reflects the L1 data used in the game and ensures that out of sync nodes are ignored. If all nodes are out of sync it is considered a fetch failure.

Conveniently this also means that when a node falls behind, rather than raising an alert because games resolved incorrectly, it will report that op-dispute-mon is failing to update games correctly which is much less scary and misleading.

op-node: update OnUnsafeL2Payload to perform ELSync gap filling

This PR is intended to disable/deprecate RR sync, and replace its functionality with a FCU call to the EL node that can also fill unsafe chain gaps.

Fixes: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/17627

---

**BEFORE**
2 modes - set via flags, default is CLSync 
1. CLSync
    1. Initial bootstrapping / sync — via L1 derivation
    2. Further sync
        1. Unsafe heads gossip — apply unsafe blocks one by one via intermediate in-memory Payloads Heap
        2. Gap filling - RR sync
    3. RR p2p sync server is running
2. ELSync
    1. Initial bootstrapping / sync — via EL node syncing (snap-sync or similar)
    2. Further sync
        1. Unsafe heads gossip — apply unsafe blocks one by one via intermediate in-memory Payloads Heap
        2. Gap filling - RR sync
    3. RR p2p sync server is not running

---

**AFTER**
2 modes - set via flags, default is CLSync 
1. CLSync
    1. Initial bootstrapping / sync — via L1 derivation
    2. Further sync
        1. Unsafe heads gossip — apply unsafe blocks one by one via intermediate in-memory Payloads Heap
        2. **(changed)** Gap filling - detection stays the same with altTicker, but filling is done directly with the EL node
    3. RR p2p sync server is not running
2. ELSync
    1. Initial bootstrapping / sync — via EL node syncing (snap-sync or similar)
    2. Further sync
        1. **(changed)** Unsafe heads gossip — apply unsafe blocks one by one directly via EL node; no longer passes through the intermediate Payloads Heap
        2. **(changed)** Gap filling - done directly via the application of unsafe heads gossip to the EL node
    3. **(changed)** RR p2p sync server is not running

---

**TESTS**

1. `TestUnsafeChainStalling_CLSync` and `TestUnsafeChainStalling_ELSync` - verifies that if an unsafe chain gap emerges, due to network issues, a node running in `CLSync` or `ELSync` mode will fill the gap and continue to advance its unsafe chain, without help from the L1 derivation pipeline.
2. `TestUnsafeChainStalling_CLSync_RestartOpNode_Long` and `TestUnsafeChainStalling_ELSync_RestartOpNode_Long` - same as 1, but with actual stopping/starting of the `op-node` and not just network issue. Verifies that if an unsafe chain gap emerges, a node running in `CLSync` or `ELSync` mode will fill the gap after booting up.
3. `TestUnsafeChainStalling_DisabledReqRespSync` - test is modified to show that the unsafe chain does not stall if RR sync is disabled, which is the case on current `develop` (i.e. we can't just switch RR sync on `develop` as is, without losing functionality)

---

**TODO**

- [ ] address `TestSyncAfterInitialELSync`.
fix(devstack/op-reth): fix devstack configuration for op-reth/networks with more than one validator

## Description

It is impossible to run sysgo with more than an op-reth node at a time. This is a fix that ensures we can:
- deploy networks with more than one op-reth node
- networks can be successfully deployed.

Rationale:
- Disabling discv4 discovery in op-reth is not enough. The former configuration would deploy op-reth with discv5 using the default address/port, which then would fail when trying to deploy more than one node and this node tries to bind to an already allocated port
- `admin_addPeer` does not _also_ connect peers automatically - manually added peers through the admin api will not appear in `admin_peers`. The check below was failing because we expected that peers added through `admin_addPeer` would also appear when calling `admin_peers`.

feat: introduce fee splitter for revenue share

**Description**

Introduce the `FeeSplitter` predeploy as part of a new revenue-sharing feature. The goal is to make revenue sharing simpler and more modular, with configurable values and automated handling where possible.

Includes supporting contracts like `SuperchainRevSharesCalculator`, `L1Withdrawer`, and `FeesDepositor`, which act as periphery components of the system and cover the first expected use case.

This is opt-in, but will be enabled by default on fresh chains at genesis. Operators must set a chain fees recipient address on L2 for splits to work.

`FeeVaults` were updated to be more flexible with setters, while keeping backwards compatibility.

* Genesis logic has dedicated tests, and there ar integration tests covering the full main flow.
* Invariant tests added using Foundry as fuzzer.

Release notes

Sourced from github.com/docker/docker's releases.

v28.0.0

28.0.0

For a full list of pull requests and changes in this release, refer to the relevant GitHub milestones:

  • docker/cli, 28.0.0 milestone
  • moby/moby, 28.0.0 milestone
  • Deprecated and removed features, see Deprecated Features.
  • Changes to the Engine API, see API version history.

New

  • Add ability to mount an image inside a container via --mount type=image. moby/moby#48798
    • You can also specify --mount type=image,image-subpath=[subpath],... option to mount a specific path from the image. docker/cli#5755
  • docker images --tree now shows metadata badges. docker/cli#5744
  • docker load, docker save, and docker history now support a --platform flag allowing you to choose a specific platform for single-platform operations on multi-platform images. docker/cli#5331
  • Add OOMScoreAdj to docker service create and docker stack. docker/cli#5145
  • docker buildx prune now supports reserved-space, max-used-space, min-free-space and keep-bytes filters. moby/moby#48720
  • Windows: Add support for running containerd as a child process of the daemon, instead of using a system-installed containerd. moby/moby#47955

Networking

  • The docker-proxy binary has been updated, older versions will not work with the updated dockerd. moby/moby#48132
    • Close a window in which the userland proxy (docker-proxy) could accept TCP connections, that would then fail after iptables NAT rules were set up.
    • The executable rootlesskit-docker-proxy is no longer used, it has been removed from the build and distribution.
  • DNS nameservers read from the host's /etc/resolv.conf are now always accessed from the host's network namespace. moby/moby#48290
    • When the host's /etc/resolv.conf contains no nameservers and there are no --dns overrides, Google's DNS servers are no longer used, apart from by the default bridge network and in build containers.
  • Container interfaces in bridge and macvlan networks now use randomly generated MAC addresses. moby/moby#48808
    • Gratuitous ARP / Neighbour Advertisement messages will be sent when the interfaces are started so that, when IP addresses are reused, they're associated with the newly generated MAC address.
    • IPv6 addresses in the default bridge network are now IPAM-assigned, rather than being derived from the MAC address.
  • The deprecated OCI prestart hook is now only used by build containers. For other containers, network interfaces are added to the network namespace after task creation is complete, before the container task is started. moby/moby#47406
  • Add a new gw-priority option to docker run, docker container create, and docker network connect. This option will be used by the Engine to determine which network provides the default gateway for a container. On docker run, this option is only available through the extended --network syntax. docker/cli#5664
  • Add a new netlabel com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname to customize the interface name used when connecting a container to a network. It's supported by all built-in network drivers on Linux. moby/moby#49155
    • When a container is created with multiple networks specified, there's no guarantee on the order networks will be connected to the container. So, if a custom interface name uses the same prefix as the auto-generated names, for example eth, the container might fail to start.
    • The recommended practice is to use a different prefix, for example en0, or a numerical suffix high enough to never collide, for example eth100.
    • This label can be specified on docker network connect via the --driver-opt flag, for example docker network connect --driver-opt=com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname=foobar ….
    • Or via the long-form --network flag on docker run, for example docker run --network=name=bridge,driver-opt=com.docker.network.endpoint.ifname=foobar …
  • If a custom network driver reports capability GwAllocChecker then, before a network is created, it will get a GwAllocCheckerRequest with the network's options. The custom driver may then reply that no gateway IP address should be allocated. moby/moby#49372

Port publishing in bridge networks

  • dockerd now requires ipset support in the Linux kernel. moby/moby#48596
    • The iptables and ip6tables rules used to implement port publishing and network isolation have been extensively modified. This enables some of the following functional changes, and is a first step in refactoring to enable native nftables support in a future release. moby/moby#48815
    • If it becomes necessary to downgrade to an earlier version of the daemon, some manual cleanup of the new rules will be necessary. The simplest and surest approach is to reboot the host, or use iptables -F and ip6tables -F to flush all existing iptables rules from the filter table before starting the older version of the daemon. When that is not possible, run the following commands as root:
      • iptables -D FORWARD -m set --match-set docker-ext-bridges-v4 dst -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT; ip6tables -D FORWARD -m set --match-set docker-ext-bridges-v6 dst -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
      • iptables -D FORWARD -m set --match-set docker-ext-bridges-v4 dst -j DOCKER; ip6tables -D FORWARD -m set --match-set docker-ext-bridges-v6 dst -j DOCKER
      • If you were previously running with the iptables filter-FORWARD policy set to ACCEPT and need to restore access to unpublished ports, also delete per-bridge-network rules from the DOCKER chains. For example, iptables -D DOCKER ! -i docker0 -o docker0 -j DROP.
  • Fix a security issue that was allowing remote hosts to connect directly to a container on its published ports. moby/moby#49325
  • Fix a security issue that was allowing neighbor hosts to connect to ports mapped on a loopback address. moby/moby#49325

**Description**

Mutexs are now fine grained, embedded per each session.

Introduce a session Manager, which abstracts locking operations for the sessions, and each session holds their own lock to protect themselves while modification.

No logic change in the sync tester APIs except explicit locking mechanism added:

For APIs we now wrap around the logic with `WithSession`. Example:
```go
func (s *SyncTester) GetBlockByNumber(ctx context.Context, number rpc.BlockNumber, fullTx bool) (json.RawMessage, error) {
	return WithSession(s.sessMgr, ctx, func(session *eth.SyncTesterSession) (json.RawMessage, error) {
		var err error
		var target uint64
		if target, err = s.checkBlockNumber(number, session); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		var raw json.RawMessage
		if raw, err = s.elReader.GetBlockByNumberJSON(ctx, rpc.BlockNumber(target), fullTx); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		return raw, nil
	})
}

```
which under the hood, acquires locks.

All locks are blocking, but they can be changed to TryLocks in the future.

All existing tests are passing.

**Additional context**

Before this PR few APIs did not properly acquire locks. This PR adds proper locking mechanisms to every APIs.

Also hardened holocene related checks(eip1559params) and tweaked error messages.

**Description**

Adds EL Sync support for sync tester.

While L2CL is configured to do EL Sync, the L2CL will optimistically signal the underlying L2EL with future blocks. The L2EL will respond `SYNCING` to the engine API(`engine_getPayload`, `engine_forkChoiceUpdate`) till the L2EL reaches the point that it can validate the optimistically added payload by the L2CL, eventually returning `VALID` response.

Sync Tester is a mock EL, and it can be configured to whether return `SYNCING` to make the L2CL think the L2EL is working to fill in the gaps, gaining ability to validate the optimistically inserted payload, or `VALID` to make the L2CL think the EL Sync is completed, and falling back to the CL Sync(or L1 Sync).

Sync Tester may now optionally initialize the session using the `el_sync_target=<uint64>` query parameter. On the happy path with sync tester configured with the `el_sync_target` plus L2CL configured to do EL Sync,
1. L2CL will receive unsafe payloads from sequencer. At this point the L2CL EL Sync is started.
2. L2CL will send `engine_getPayload`, `engine_forkChoiceUpdate` to the Sync Tester and receive `SYNCING`
3. Sequencer will eventually send the payload which the block number is equal to the `el_sync_target`.
4. L2CL will send `engine_getPayload`, `engine_forkChoiceUpdate` to the Sync Tester and receive `VALID`. At this point the L2CL EL Sync is finished.
5. L2CL will start CL Sync(or L1 Sync).

Note that `el_sync_target` cannot be set less that `latest`, and handled as an error when initializing session. It makes no sense since when `el_sync_target < latest`, EL sync has been already done.

**Tests**

The happy path test is added at `TestSyncTesterELSync`.

Note that the L2CL connected to Sync Tester must have L2 P2P enabled, connected to the sequencer. L2CL must be signaled with new latest unsafe head, to trigger and finish EL Sync.

**Additional context**

Adds a new API `sync_resetSession` to intentionally roll back the sync tester session to initial state, making gaps between `latest` and `el_sync_target`.

Fixes a bug in `engine_newPayload` implementation; previously all three heads(latest, safe, finalized) where atomically updated together. This behavior mismatched with op-geth, causing EL Sync to fail. 

Ideas: It would be nice to enhance the observability that the op-node is doing EL Sync, or CL Sync. Currently no internal state is exposed for this.

op-batcher: decrement pending bytes metrics when pruning pending blocks

This can happen if there is a race between a fresh batcher loading a block (it becomes pending initially) and a sequencer ingesting a transaction which makes that block safe. It then gets pruned despite being _pending_, and we are forgetting to update key metrics when this happens.

This could happen during a restart of the batcher, since blocks which were in channels essentially become pending again for a short time. It is in effect a sort of rewind of the batcher's data pipeline, and we aren't binding metrics update to that event. 

Towards https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/14559

Remove event mediation from new unsafe payload logic

**Summary:**
Refactors unsafe payload processing to use direct method calls instead of event-driven architecture, simplifying the codebase and improving performance.

**Key Changes:**
- **CLSync**: Replaces event handlers with direct `AddUnsafePayload()` and `ProcessReadyPayloads()` methods
- **Sequencer**: Now calls `engine.ProcessPayload()` directly instead of emitting `ProcessUnsafePayloadEvent`

**Benefits:**
- Eliminates event emission/handling overhead
- Enables synchronous error handling and immediate retry logic  
- Reduces complexity by removing event coordination between components
- More predictable execution flow with direct method calls

**Test coverage:** All existing tests updated and new test cases added

**Removes Events:**
- ReceivedUnsafePayloadEvent
- ProcessUnsafePayloadEvent
- ForkchoiceRequestEvent

---

This refactoring maintains the same functionality while moving from an asynchronous event-driven model to a simpler synchronous direct-call model for unsafe payload processing.
op-batcher: support throttling additional endpoints (e.g. builders participating in a rollup-boost setup)

Replaces #14859 

Changes the batcher behavior to always throttle all sequencer EL endpoints, plus any additional endpoints specified by a new CLI flag. Throttling is performed on each endpoint concurrently and mostly independently. 

For context, see this design doc https://github.com/worldcoin/rollup-boost/blob/rollup-boost-ha/docs/rollup-boost-ha.md. 

TODO
- [x] still an open question as to whether we need a _separate_ list of throttling endpoints in the config (in addition to the existing comma separated list of eth rpc endpoints / sequencers). If we can get away with the existing list, it would simplify the code a bit. 

---
It became clear that we do need the separate list.

- the builder can build L2 blocks which can end up becoming canonical, so it needs to be throttled
- the builder does not serve those blocks over Ethereum JSON-RPC, so it doesn't make sense to add it as an endpoint for the batcher to fetch blocks from
- a block from the builder (which works as a sidecar) will actually end up in the "proposer" op-geth instance (aka the sequencer in rollup-boost mode) via the engine-API orchestration enabled by rollup-boost. And the batcher can pull that block from the proposer op-geth, which it does have in it's list of endpoints
I came to this conclusion by reading this readme https://github.com/flashbots/rollup-boost . We need the additional flag to represent the different relationship between batcher and builder (compared to batcher and sequencer).

# ci: Add nightly heavy fuzz testing job

## Summary

Adds a new nightly CI job that runs comprehensive smart contract fuzz tests using the `ciheavy` Foundry profile (20,000 fuzz runs, 128 invariant runs, 512 depth) to catch edge cases that regular CI might miss.

**Key changes:**
- New `contracts-bedrock-heavy-fuzz-nightly` job using `ciheavy` profile with 90m timeout
- New `scheduled-heavy-fuzz-tests` workflow triggered nightly via `build_daily` schedule 
- Added `heavy_fuzz_dispatch` parameter for manual testing
- Job tests ALL contracts in `packages/contracts-bedrock`, not just modified files

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Critical: Verify test-rerun step uses `ci` profile** - The cumulative diff shows it using `ciheavy` but PR feedback requested `ci` for cleaner failure traces
- [ ] **Test manual dispatch functionality** - Use CircleCI UI to trigger via `heavy_fuzz_dispatch` parameter before waiting for nightly schedule
- [ ] **Monitor first nightly run** - Check for timeouts (90m might be insufficient) and resource constraints (xlarge might need upgrade to 2xlarge)
- [ ] **Verify nightly scheduling works** - Confirm job actually runs at 2 AM UTC via `build_daily` schedule after merge
- [ ] **Check Slack notifications** - Ensure failure notifications work properly with the `slack` context

**Description**

There are multiple control flows which invokes Engine Controller logic. Some subroutines will be invoked starting from events, namely `onEvent`, and it properly acquires RW mutex which is embedded in EngineController struct.

The current codebase does not properly acquire mutexes while modifying the state of the EngineController. This may lead to potential race conditions.

The root of the current mis-synchronization stems from two reasons. 
1. While we were refactoring op-node, proper synchronization was missed. When we replace the events with synchronous function calls, the function call itself loses locking. Therefore we need an explicit locking while removing the events.
    - ex) https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/17165: `PromoteFinalizedEvent` was replaced with function, and mutex locking got removed. The `Finalizer` struct directly called engine controller subroutine.
    - ex) https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/16941: `PromotePendingSafeEvent`, `PromoteLocalSafeEvent` was replaced with function, and mutex locking got removed. `AttributeHandler` struct directly called engine controller subroutine.
    - ex) https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/17096: Some direct struct embeddings at `s.Engine.TryUpdateEngine` at SyncDeriver.
    - ex) `ForceReset(ctx context.Context, localUnsafe, crossUnsafe, localSafe, crossSafe, finalized eth.L2BlockRef)` 
2. Existing subroutines which were not handled correctly. 
    - ex) `EngineController.IsEngineSyncing()` was invoked outside the engine controller, at SyncDeriver without read lock.
   

Upper lists are non-exhaustive. 

The easy way to check the engine controller subroutines entrypoint is to search `type EngineController interface` throughout the codebase. This PR attempts to apply proper mutex locking.

If possible, the exposure of these methods should be minimized.

Will follow up on the other subroutines.

Possibly related with the race conditions reported at https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/17564

The motivation behind this change is that `clsync.CLSync` provides very little / trivial functionality, namely:
- it manages a heap of unsafe blocks received over p2p
- it tries to apply the highest block number payload

`clsync.CLSync` is also coupled with `engine.EngineController`.

Merging the two reduces the number of components we have to keep in mind, and also allows for further simplifications.

---

1. Merge `clsync.CLSync` with `engine.EngineController`
2. Remove `ProcessUnsafePayload` event in favor of a simple function call.
3. Remove `onPayloadInvalid`.
4. Removed unused interfaces.
5. Consistently used direct fields instead of Getters from within the same value (`*EngineController`), instead of a mix of these two.
6. Removed unused Getters for `EngineController`.
7. Refactored tests under `clsync_test.go` and moved under `engine_controller_test.go`

Since [Ecotone](https://specs.optimism.io/protocol/ecotone/l1-attributes.html), the L1BlockInfo deposit transaction couples the L2 state transition with the blob base fee of the l1 origin. The blob base fee is not part of the block, but rather computed from `block.excessBlobGas` with an [off-chain formula which varies according to which fork is active on L1.](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/blob/51614a3dc4af4a2b503ba178e0799013e6774613/consensus/misc/eip4844/eip4844.go#L180-L197)

For the L2 state to accurately reflect the blob base fee of the l1 origin, it is necessary to provide the L2 consensus client information about the fork schedule of the L1 which it derives from.

This PR does that in a relatively lightweight way:
* for chains with a recognized l1 chain ID (such as all chains in the superchain registry), lookup the l1 chain config (either for Mainnet or Sepolia) using op-geth as a library. This information needs to be kept updated as new L1 forks (including BPO or blob parameter only forks) are scheduled in upstream geth and brought in through upstream merges. When this happens, we need to update the absolute prestate for the proofs system
* for custom chains (think devnets, test environments, chains which are not in the superchain registry) it is required to pass the l1 chain config via a new CLI flag. This can be directly JSON encoded or embedded in a `genesis.json` file.
* Does something similar for the op-program, which does not allow information to be passed at runtime but instead via filesystem embedding
* Also includes changes in this direction for kona

I avoided embedding the l1 chain config inside the `rollup.Config`, as that would require changing all of the data in the superchain registry.

This is a backwards compatible change which also makes the derivation pipeline compatible with post-Fusaka L1s.

The diff is quite large, mostly because there is a lot of boilerplate to change both in production and test code.

Closes #17493

op-node: Do not set unsafe head while payload is syncing

<!--
Contributions welcome! See https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/.github/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

**Description**

While we EL Sync,  op-node receives new payloads, and attempts to tell the EL. It loops using below steps until the EL is ready(returning `VALID`):
1. Call `engine_newPayload`, and EL yet synced so response is `SYNCING`.
2. Call `engine_forkchoiceupdated`, and EL yet synced to response is `SYNCING`.

While op-node waits till the EL is ready, and returns `VALID` response to the engine APIs, op-node's `syncStatus`(response of `optimism_syncStatus` must not be updated since the underlying EL is not yet synced.

This PR fixes the case that when op-node is operating in EL Sync, and connected EL is not yet fully synced (returning `SYNCING` and not `VALID`), op-node updated its unsafe head view.

Require that msgSender be an owner of the Safe

This PR enhances the security of the TimelockGuard by adding a check that requires the `msgSender` to be an owner of the Safe before allowing transaction execution. This prevents attackers from executing transactions even if they manage to collect valid signatures, as they would also need to control a private key of a Safe owner. # refactor(test): improve SafeSend test coverage and quality

## Summary
Converted SafeSend tests from fixed-value tests to fuzz tests for broader coverage and added edge case testing for address(0) transfers. The SafeSend contract uses selfdestruct to send ETH without executing recipient code.

**Changes:**
- Converted `test_constructor_toEOA_succeeds` to fuzz test with amounts from 0 to `type(uint192).max`
- Converted `test_constructor_toContract_succeeds` to fuzz test with same range  
- Added `testFuzz_constructor_toZeroAddress_succeeds` to test edge case of sending to address(0)

**Bound Reasoning:**
Initially used `type(uint128).max`, then removed bounds per reviewer feedback, but unbounded fuzzing caused arithmetic overflow in test balance calculations (`aliceBalanceBefore - _amount` when `_amount ≈ type(uint256).max`). Settled on `type(uint192).max` as a compromise:
- Provides enormous test range (~6.3e57, far exceeding total ETH supply ~1.2e26)
- Prevents overflow in test environment's balance tracking
- Note: The overflow is a test limitation, not a contract issue

All tests verify:
1. SafeSend contract is destroyed (code length = 0, balance = 0)  
2. Sender balance decreases by sent amount
3. Recipient balance increases by sent amount

- [ ] Validate address(0) test is meaningful - does sending to address(0) via selfdestruct behave as expected?

<!--
Contributions welcome! See https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/.github/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md

**Description**

Added three tests, which demonstrates that the op-node can follow the unsafe tip of the sequencer by filling in the gap.

The gap-filling method is currently done by the ReqRes sync, and it will be substituted by Multiple EL Sync which is implemented at [op-node: update OnUnsafeL2Payload to perform ELSync gap filling](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/17751).

This means, if this PR is first merged then then [op-node: update OnUnsafeL2Payload to perform ELSync gap filling](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/17751) is merged, the **tests should still pass for both syncmodes: `sync.ELSync` and `sync.CLSync` since both options will allow multiple EL Syncs**.

**Tests**

The tests leverage the `TestSequencer`, which can trigger L1 reorg, leading L2 {safe|unsafe} reorg. All three test case use RR Sync to fill in the unsafe gap. 

#### `TestUnsafeGapFillAfterSafeReorg`

```
// TestUnsafeGapFillAfterSafeReorg demonstrates the sequence:
//  1. Verifier CLP2P is disconnected and Verifier CL is stopped.
//  2. Safe reorg occurs because L1 reorged.
//  3. Verifier restarts, and consolidation drops the verifier previously-unsafe blocks.
//  4. CLP2P is restored, the verifier backfills and the unsafe gap is closed.
```

#### `TestUnsafeGapFillAfterUnsafeReorg_RestartL2CL`

```
// TestUnsafeGapFillAfterUnsafeReorg_RestartL2CL demonstrates the flow where:
//  1. Verifier L2CL is stopped.
//  2. Unsafe reorg occurs because L1 reorged,
//  3. Verifier restarts and detects the L1 reorg, triggering its own unsafe reorg,
//  4. Verifier then backfills and closes the unsafe gap once reconnected via CLP2P.
```

#### `TestUnsafeGapFillAfterUnsafeReorg_RestartCLP2P`

```
// TestUnsafeGapFillAfterUnsafeReorg_RestartCLP2P demonstrates the flow where:
//  1. Verifier CLP2P is disconnected.
//  2. Unsafe reorg occurs because L1 reorged.
//  3. Verifier detects the L1 reorg, triggering its own unsafe reorg.
//  4. CLP2P is restored Verifier, the verifier backfills and the unsafe gap is closed.
```

**Additional Context**

About the flakiness of newly added tests: At https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism?branch=pcw109550%2Facceptance-test-sync-reorg I triggered acceptance tests pipeline 8 times, and newly added tests never flaked.

interop: validate PendingProgress equals number of chains during consolidation

Problem: Consolidation assumed a 1:1 mapping between superRoot.Chains and transitionState.PendingProgress but only checked len(PendingProgress) > ConsolidateStep (127). This allowed inconsistent lengths, risking out-of-range access or silent misalignment during consolidation where PendingProgress[i] is indexed per chain.

Fix: Replace the check with len(transitionState.PendingProgress) == len(superRoot.Chains) and emit a precise error message including both lengths. This enforces the actual invariant required by RunConsolidation and related logic.

fix: make LookupSymbol use exclusive end boundary

Update LookupSymbol to treat the symbol end as exclusive by changing the gap check from out.Start+out.Size < addr to addr >= out.Start+out.Size. This aligns with:
- ELF symbol semantics where [start, start+size) is standard
- Our CreateSymbolMatcher, which already uses a half-open interval

Previously, addr == start+size could be incorrectly attributed to the preceding symbol, leading to inaccurate symbol lookups at function boundaries and inconsistent behavior in stack tracing and debugging. This change ensures consistent, correct address-to-symbol mapping across the codebase.

This initial PR for `op-supernode` introduces a core functionality: Chain Containers. Chain containers allow for multi-tenant Consensus Layer. The initial functionality of the `op-supernode` is to serve multiple CLs from a shared binary using shared resources. ## PR Breakdown - How to Review This PR is larger than I wanted it to be, but contains a solid unit of functionality: The ability to run multiple CLs inside a containerized system. The code breaks down into more reviewable sections: ### op-node - The only change to `op-node` is additional initialization to accept overloaded resources. This is used to create dependency-injected Virtual Nodes with shared resources. The overloads were made available in a prior PR and now being utilized. Additional refactor to the `cliiface` was added to expand a prior refactor I had done, where the `cli.Context` object is replaced. ### Acceptance Tests and Devstack - A new preset for 2 L2 networks bound by a Supernode is created - A new "TestL2CLAdvance Multiple" test which confirms two different networks advance from the same supernode. ### Supervisor A lot of Supervisor is CLi and Boilerplate, but here's why each component exists: - `supernode` is the primary Application Lifecycle, and manages Chain Containers - `chain_containers` hold chain-specific configuration and ensure a Virtual Node is always running - `virtual_node` wrap an underlying CL - `shared_clients` creates wrapped version of common resources (L1 clients) which the virtual nodes can't close - `http router` handles top level RPC and routes the calls down to the virtual nodes using a chainID supplied in the url - `virtual_flags` and `virtual_cli` namespaces the incoming CLI in order to implement a wrapped CLI Context which *appears* normal to the virtual nodes, allowing for 1:1 identical startup, including environment variables and defaults. ## Tests - Unit Test coverage on Virtual Node and Chain Container Lifecycle Management - Unit Test coverage on virtualized cli and flags - Unit test coverage on the http router - Acceptance Test coverage of advancing multiple chains - Manual testing of multi-chain syncing of `op-sepolia` and `base-sepolia` including RPC access: # Milestone 1 Closes/Satisfies[ Milestone 1](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/17558)

   ```toml
    challenger = "0x9ba6e03d8b90de867373db8cf1a58d2f7f006b3a"

   ```

4. Attempt to deploy using genesis target:

   ```bash
   op-deployer apply --workdir ./test-standard --deployment-target genesis
   ```

5. Observe error: "superchain roles must be set for genesis strategy"

6. Add superchain roles to intent.toml:

   ```toml
   [superchainRoles]
   SuperchainProxyAdminOwner = "0x5a0aae59d09fccbddb6c6cceb07b7279367c3d2a"
   SuperchainGuardian = "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000009"
   ProtocolVersionsOwner = "0x000000000000000000000000000000000000000b"
   Challenger = "0x9ba6e03d8b90de867373db8cf1a58d2f7f006b3a"
   ```

7. Observe new error: "chain contains incompatible config value"

**Expected behavior**

Should be able to deploy a standard chain using the genesis target without configuration conflicts. The validation rules should be consistent between deployment targets and intent types.

**Additional context**

The issue stems from conflicting validations in:

1. [`pipeline/init.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/96b920867c086b8568156d98b092246f5eccbb9d/op-deployer/pkg/deployer/pipeline/init.go#L115-#L117): `InitGenesisStrategy` requires superchain roles for genesis deployment.

   ```go
   if intent.SuperchainRoles == nil {
       return fmt.Errorf("superchain roles must be set for genesis strategy")
   }
   ```

2. [`state/intent.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/96b920867c086b8568156d98b092246f5eccbb9d/op-deployer/pkg/deployer/state/intent.go#L145-#L147): `validateStandardValues` rejects superchain roles for standard intent type.

   ```go
   if c.SuperchainRoles != nil {
       return ErrIncompatibleValue
   }
   ```

**Proposed Solution**

Remove the superchain roles validation for standard intent type in `state/intent.go`.

The `pipeline/init.go` check remains as the superchain roles are required for executing `DeploySuperchain` function.

**Note**: This change only affects the genesis deployment target. The live deployment target (`InitLiveStrategy`) is unaffected because:

1.  For standard intent type, `validateStandardValues` requires OPCM address to be set.

2.  When OPCM address is set, [`InitLiveStrategy`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/55150e4898ccf845735de83e98a76871922e0ef0/op-deployer/pkg/deployer/pipeline/init.go#L36) requires SuperchainRoles to be set too:

```go
if hasPredeployedOPCM {
   //...
   if intent.SuperchainRoles != nil {
   return fmt.Errorf("cannot set superchain roles for predeployed OPCM")
   }
}
```

# docs(specs): improve GovernanceToken specification

## Summary

This PR significantly expands the GovernanceToken specification from a minimal 73-line document to a comprehensive 595-line specification that follows the canonical OP Stack spec format. The original spec was incomplete - it only documented 3 functions and lacked critical sections like Invariants, Assumptions, and Dependencies.

**Key additions:**
- **Definitions section**: Added formal definitions for Voting Power, Delegation, and Checkpoint
- **Assumptions section**: Documented 4 external dependencies (MintManager enforcement, OpenZeppelin correctness, user understanding, governance query correctness)
- **Invariants section**: Identified 8 core system properties with severity ratings (4 Critical, 2 High, 2 Medium)
- **Dependencies section**: Links to ERC20, ERC20Permit, ERC20Votes, ERC20Burnable, and Ownable
- **Function specifications**: Complete specs for all 23 functions (mint, burn, delegation, voting queries, ERC20 standard, ERC20Permit)

**Critical bug fixes:**
- Fixed `getVotes()` signature - spec said `getVotes()` but actual function is `getVotes(address account)`
- Added missing documentation for EIP-2612 permit functionality
- Documented uint224 max supply constraint that prevents overflow
- Added checkpoint structure details (fromBlock uint32, votes uint224)

The specification is now complete enough that a developer could implement the GovernanceToken contract from this spec alone without needing to reference the Solidity code.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Verify invariants are goals, not tactics**: Review the 8 invariants (iGT-001 through iGT-008) and confirm each describes *what must be true* rather than *how it's implemented*. Example: iGT-003 says "Voting power accurately reflects delegated balances" (goal) rather than "Checkpoints are updated on transfers" (tactic).

- [ ] **Spot-check function specs against contract**: Pick 3-5 functions and verify the specification matches the actual GovernanceToken.sol implementation at `/optimism/packages/contracts-bedrock/src/governance/GovernanceToken.sol`. Pay special attention to inherited functions from OpenZeppelin contracts.

- [ ] **Validate `getVotes()` signature fix**: Confirm the function signature is `getVotes(address account)` not `getVotes()` in the OpenZeppelin ERC20Votes contract. The original spec had this wrong.

- [ ] **Review severity ratings**: Check that the Critical/High/Medium severity assignments for the 8 invariants make sense. Critical ratings were assigned to mint authorization, burn authorization, voting power accuracy, and historical immutability.

### Notes

- This is a documentation-only change - no contract code was modified
- All linting checks pass (markdown formatting, TOC, spelling)
- Spec was written by analyzing GovernanceToken.sol and inherited OpenZeppelin contracts (ERC20Burnable, ERC20Votes, ERC20Permit, Ownable)
- The uint224 max supply constraint is enforced by ERC20Votes to prevent checkpoint overflow

fix(op-alt-da): ensure HTTP response bodies are closed in error cases

## Summary

Fixes a resource leak in `op-alt-da/daclient.go` by ensuring HTTP response bodies are properly closed in all error scenarios.

## Problem

The `GetInput` method in `DAClient` was not closing HTTP response bodies when returning early due to error status codes (404, non-200). This can lead to:
- Resource leaks and file descriptor exhaustion
- Performance degradation due to inability to reuse connections
- Potential connection pool exhaustion under load

## Solution

Moved `defer resp.Body.Close()` immediately after the `client.Do(req)` call to guarantee response body closure in all execution paths, including error cases.

# Create MintManager Specification

## Summary

This PR adds a comprehensive specification for the `MintManager` contract (`src/governance/MintManager.sol`), which controls governance token inflation. The spec follows the canonical OP Stack format with:

- **2 definitions**: Mint Cap (2%) and Mint Period (365 days) - referenced throughout via markdown links
- **4 assumptions**: GovernanceToken implementation, block timestamp reliability, owner governance behavior, valid successor
- **4 invariants**: Mint cap enforcement (Medium), time-based restrictions (Medium), exclusive authority (Critical), ownership control (Critical)
- **3 function specifications**: constructor, mint, upgrade with MUST/MUST NOT requirements

**Important divergence**: The spec documents INTENDED behavior where all mints have restrictions. The current contract has a bug where the first mint (`mintPermittedAfter == 0`) bypasses checks. Per reviewer, the spec should describe desired future behavior and the contract will be fixed later.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

This is a **yellow risk** PR (documentation only, but accuracy is critical):

- [ ] **Verify intentional spec-to-contract divergence is acceptable**: Spec states all mints have restrictions (lines 116-158), but current contract allows first mint to bypass checks (see `if (mintPermittedAfter > 0)` in `MintManager.sol:46-53`). Confirm documenting intended future behavior is correct approach.
- [ ] **Verify constants exactly match contract**: Check that MINT_CAP = 20, DENOMINATOR = 1000 (2%), MINT_PERIOD = 365 days match `MintManager.sol:21-28` character-for-character
- [ ] **Validate severity ratings**: Review whether Medium (not Critical) is appropriate for iMM-001 and iMM-002, given they require governance assumption (aMM-003) to fail. Reviewer iterated: Critical → High → Medium.
- [ ] **Confirm invariants are goals, not tactics**: Read iMM-001 through iMM-004 (lines 115-195) and verify they state "what must be true" rather than "how it's implemented"
- [ ] **Verify completeness**: Confirm all public/external functions from MintManager.sol are documented (constructor, mint, upgrade)

fix: resolve race condition in ThrottleController.Update method

Fix race condition in ThrottleController.Update by changing RLock to Lock

The Update method was using RLock to read strategy reference, then calling
strategy.Update() without holding the lock. This created a race condition
where SetStrategy could change the strategy between reading the reference
and using it, leading to inconsistent throttling behavior.

Using Lock instead of RLock ensures the entire Update operation is atomic,
preventing SetStrategy from modifying the strategy while Update executes.
This guarantees thread safety when controller type is changed at runtime.

<!-- Contributions welcome! See https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/.github/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

**Description**

Adds config to enable XFF verification, which compares the last IP in the XFF address list against the remote address (client IP). This protects against IP spoofing, which attackers can use to exhaust rate limits of other IPs.

Proxyd will automatically disable this verification if the rate limit header is overridden to not be `x-forwarded-for`.

**Tests**

Unit tests added for all new code

**Additional context**

```
Sender Verification
It is possible that attackers might connect to proxyd directly in misconfigured deployments.

To ensure correct functioning proxyd should verify that the last entry in the x-forwarded-for chain is equal to the connection initiator. Without such a check the trust chain control would be less effective, as an attacker could simply mirror a request as if it has the expected trusted proxy IP addresses.
```

**Description**

Max block range config to limit block range for potentially expensive rpc requests like `eth_getLogs` and `eth_newFilter`. The config applies across all routing strategies, and will only be applied if the config value is set. Otherwise, it reverts to original behavior, with no limits.

Note, if `max_block_range` is set, the above two requests will not accept block tags, to prevent unbounded queries.

**Tests**

Integration test for `eth_getLogs` to test that the config value is working as intended.

**Additional context**

This is from a Spearbit audit in Cantina that Unichain recently did.

```
Description
Some operations like eth_getLogs can take quite a while, especially if a user requests abnormally large block ranges.

This can be problematic when the proxyd service considers a timeout of 5 seconds for any requests that it has forwarded. It will mark down an error case if any backend takes longer than 5 seconds to service such a request. A backend with too many errors will eventually be considered an "unhealthy" backend and proxyd will stop using that backend.

A user can intentionally send many requests that result in a timeout. This is the cae because the nodes used in the Unichain deployment do not have limits configured needed to ensure that nodes are able to guarantee the 5 second latency contract that proxyd expects.

Executing this approach on a large scale can cause proxyd to consider an entire backend group as unhealthy, and stop servicing (some) legitimate requests.

Recommendation
Execute a range of simple benchmarks that can be used to inform an initial set of limits for the rpc calls that are prone to long execution times.

An alternative approach is to leverage monitoring of the RPC nodes and basing the limits on historical observations.

It might also be possible to leverage the existing monitoring stack to detect attacks attempting to exploit this flaw.
```

The specification follows the canonical OP Stack format with:
- **Overview**: High-level description of the contract's role
- **Definitions**: Minimum Withdrawal Amount and Withdrawal Network

fix(op-node): respect sequencer.max-safe-lag stall in onForkchoiceUpdate

The sequencer’s safe-lag stall was ineffective. In onForkchoiceUpdate, when the safe head lagged beyond sequencer.max-safe-lag, we set nextActionOK=false to stall, but later unconditionally set nextActionOK=true when the unsafe head advanced, overwriting the stall. This contradicted the documented intent to “delay creating new blocks until the safe lag is below the threshold.”

This change ensures we only set nextActionOK=true and schedule the next action when the safe-to-unsafe lag is within the configured threshold. If the lag exceeds the threshold, we keep the stall active and do not modify nextAction. v0.49.0

In this release, we added support for HTTP client traces. We also fixed a large number of bugs that could lead to connection stalls, deadlocks and memory leaks. See the "Major Fixes" section for more details.

New Features

  • http3: add support for client traces net/http/httptrace.ClientTrace: #4749. Thanks to @​lRoccoon for the contribution!

Major Fixes

  • fix accounting for lost RESET_STREAM frames in the stream, leading to potential connection stalls / deadlocks: #4804. Thanks to @​Wondertan for reporting and testing the fix!
  • fix memory leak when the connection ID is rotated when the CONNECTION_CLOSE packet is sent: #4852. Thanks to @​MarcoPolo for debugging this issue and contributing a fix!
  • http3: fix QUIC connection re-dialing logic: #4854, #4875, #4879
  • trigger sending of a new packet when a MAX_DATA frame (connection-level flow control update) is queued: #4844
  • Transport.Close was reworked: calls to Transport.Dial are now canceled, and return the newly introduced ErrTransportClosed, as do calls to Transport.Listen: #4883

Enhancements

  • trace dropping of packets by the Transport when no server is set: #4789
  • trace dropping of packets that the Transport doesn't send a stateless for: #4826
  • drain received packets when the connection is closed: #4773
  • add Prometheus metrics for sent and received packets: #4910
  • reduce calls to time.Now all over the code base: #4731, #4885, #4886, #4906
  • packetize DATA_BLOCKED frames in the same QUIC packet that caused us to block on connection-level flow control: #4845
  • packetize STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frames in the same QUIC packed that caused us to block on stream-level flow control: #4801
  • we now don't enforce that only one Transport listens on any given net.PacketConn: #4851

Other Fixes

  • drain the server's connection accept queue before returning ErrClosed from Accept: #4846. Thanks to @​sukunrt for discovering this bug and providing very helpful reviews!
  • preserve the error returned from SendStream.Write if it is closed after is canceled: #4882
  • fix race condition on concurrent calls to Transport.Dial and Transport.Close: #4904
  • qlog: fix logging of packet_in_flight on the metrics_updated event: #4895
  • fix errors.Is error comparisons: #4824, #4825, #4877
  • http3: fix race condition on concurrent calls to http.Response.Body.Close: #4798. Thanks to @​RPRX for the contribution!
  • flowcontrol: reset the connection send window on 0-RTT rejection: #4764
  • wait for connection to shut down when the Dial context is cancelled: #4872
  • http3: the http.Request.Body is now properly closed on all code paths that return a non-nil error: #4874
  • NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames are now rejected when zero-length connection IDs are used, as required by the RFC: #4878
  • the stream ID of STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frames is now validated, as required by the RFC: #4836
  • fix ECN markings of packets sent in GSO batches when the marking changes: #4835
  • the AEAD used to calculate the Retry Integrity Tag is now created lazily, avoiding a panic on initialization when using Go 1.24 FIPS-only mode: #4916
  • use a 24h maximum token age as default value for Transport.MaxTokenAge: #4763

<!-- Contributions welcome! See https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/.github/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md -->

**Description**

Proxyd bans backends based on its error rate.
But it even counts context canceled error as a forwarding error,
while the cancellation is actually triggered by incomplete HTTP requests from the client.

This means hackers can make DoS attacks by just sendinga bunch of requests and closing without waiting for a response.

**Tests**

We have an environment that client sends a lot this kind of requests to test connection or some thing.
**Before this patch:**
  the proxy will have no backends to serve in a very short time.
**After:**
  works like a charm.

BTW:
`wrapErr()` will strip the error's type.
It's recommended to use [this package](https://github.com/pkg/errors) to do error wrapping and assertion.

op-node/p2p: prevent single peer failure from cancelling range sync

## Description
#10063  cancels the entire rangeRequest when any peer returns ResultCodeNotFoundErr. This forces all peers to stop working on that range and wait for the next alt-sync tick, increasing time-to-sync. In static peer setups where some peers may not yet have the requested blocks (e.g., backup sequencers or RPC nodes), a single NotFound from one peer cancels the range and unnecessarily stalls others.

## Fix
Make NotFound handling peer-local instead of global:

1. **Remove global `activeRangeRequests` tracking**: The original implementation used a global `activeRangeRequests` map to track active ranges and would delete the entire range when any peer returned NotFound, causing all peers to stop processing that range.

2. **Add peer-local `failedRanges` tracking**: Each `peerLoop` now maintains its own goroutine-local `failedRanges` map keyed by `rangeReqId`. When a peer returns NotFound for a range, we mark only that peer as failed for that range and skip subsequent blocks in that range to that specific peer.

3. **Preserve parallel syncing**: Other peers continue syncing the same range immediately without waiting for the next alt-sync tick, maximizing throughput in multi-peer setups.

This approach eliminates unnecessary global coordination, reduces memory overhead (no shared mutex-protected map), and allows healthy peers to continue syncing even when some peers don't have the requested blocks yet.

v0.49.0

In this release, we added support for HTTP client traces. We also fixed a large number of bugs that could lead to connection stalls, deadlocks and memory leaks. See the "Major Fixes" section for more details.

New Features

  • http3: add support for client traces net/http/httptrace.ClientTrace: #4749. Thanks to @​lRoccoon for the contribution!

Major Fixes

  • fix accounting for lost RESET_STREAM frames in the stream, leading to potential connection stalls / deadlocks: #4804. Thanks to @​Wondertan for reporting and testing the fix!
  • fix memory leak when the connection ID is rotated when the CONNECTION_CLOSE packet is sent: #4852. Thanks to @​MarcoPolo for debugging this issue and contributing a fix!
  • http3: fix QUIC connection re-dialing logic: #4854, #4875, #4879
  • trigger sending of a new packet when a MAX_DATA frame (connection-level flow control update) is queued: #4844
  • Transport.Close was reworked: calls to Transport.Dial are now canceled, and return the newly introduced ErrTransportClosed, as do calls to Transport.Listen: #4883

Enhancements

  • trace dropping of packets by the Transport when no server is set: #4789
  • trace dropping of packets that the Transport doesn't send a stateless for: #4826
  • drain received packets when the connection is closed: #4773
  • add Prometheus metrics for sent and received packets: #4910
  • reduce calls to time.Now all over the code base: #4731, #4885, #4886, #4906
  • packetize DATA_BLOCKED frames in the same QUIC packet that caused us to block on connection-level flow control: #4845
  • packetize STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frames in the same QUIC packed that caused us to block on stream-level flow control: #4801
  • we now don't enforce that only one Transport listens on any given net.PacketConn: #4851

Other Fixes

  • drain the server's connection accept queue before returning ErrClosed from Accept: #4846. Thanks to @​sukunrt for discovering this bug and providing very helpful reviews!
  • preserve the error returned from SendStream.Write if it is closed after is canceled: #4882
  • fix race condition on concurrent calls to Transport.Dial and Transport.Close: #4904
  • qlog: fix logging of packet_in_flight on the metrics_updated event: #4895
  • fix errors.Is error comparisons: #4824, #4825, #4877
  • http3: fix race condition on concurrent calls to http.Response.Body.Close: #4798. Thanks to @​RPRX for the contribution!
  • flowcontrol: reset the connection send window on 0-RTT rejection: #4764
  • wait for connection to shut down when the Dial context is cancelled: #4872
  • http3: the http.Request.Body is now properly closed on all code paths that return a non-nil error: #4874
  • NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames are now rejected when zero-length connection IDs are used, as required by the RFC: #4878
  • the stream ID of STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frames is now validated, as required by the RFC: #4836
  • fix ECN markings of packets sent in GSO batches when the marking changes: #4835
  • the AEAD used to calculate the Retry Integrity Tag is now created lazily, avoiding a panic on initialization when using Go 1.24 FIPS-only mode: #4916
  • use a 24h maximum token age as default value for Transport.MaxTokenAge: #4763

ci: Put go tests on regular runners

We originally made self-hosted runners for our Go tests to improve performance. Building the Go tests and downloading the caches and dependencies added up to a significant amount of test runtime. Since then, CircleCI has made a bunch of performance improvements (like zstd compression) that reduce the performance impact of those steps and make using the built-in CircleCI runners viable again.

Additionally, last week we experienced very slow builds as a result of a large build backlog. Builds were queuing due to limited self-hosted runner capacity. It would be very expensive for us to increase that capacity to where we need it.

This PR moves the Go tests back to CircleCI runners. This allows us to infinitely scale runner capacity, and obviates the need to continue maintaining the large Go test runners on Latitude. As part of this PR, I increased parallelism on the go-test-* jobs to take advantage of CircleCI's built-in sharding mechanism, and removed the code that manually distributed tests over executors in op-e2e. I used Stefano's previous attempt at test sharding to do this.

`go-tests-short` takes about 5 minutes now; with a few optimizations this could be reduced even further.

Co-Authored-By: @scharissis
op-acceptance-tests: add test to base gate for unsafe gossip / head progression

We recently realised that acceptance tests do not give us good coverage for unsafe head progression via p2p gossip. See, for example, https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/17940 (a bug which wasn't caught by ATs) as well as a recent op-reth bug we only caught on devnet. 

This test adds that coverage, and simply asserts that a) there are some non-sequencer verifier nodes and b) they catch up to the sequencer within a timeout period. 

The test disables the sysgo batcher, because otherwise safe chain derivation would allow the test to pass even if gossip was broken. Therefore this test should not run against external networks. 

I confirmed manually that introducing a bug, where op-node just rejects gossip payloads unconditionally, does indeed cause this test to fail.

eth, cmd: add RollupNetrestrictTxPoolGossipFlag PoC using `NilPool`

<!--
Contributions welcome! See https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/.github/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

**Description**

PoC implementation of RollupNetrestrictTxPoolGossip built on top of https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/pull/706.

Rationale:

Using `NilPool` worked fine for implementing notxgossip feature.
```go
	if h.noTxGossip {
		return &NilPool{}
	}
```

Instead of peer manage every inbound/outbound connection, we may make initialization of txpool ip aware, from `TxPool() TxPool` to `TxPool(ip netip.Addr) TxPool`.

```go
func (h *ethHandler) TxPool(ip netip.Addr) eth.TxPool {
	if h.noTxGossip {
		return &NilPool{}
	}
	if h.txGossipNetRestrict == nil {
		return h.txpool
	}
	if h.txGossipNetRestrict.ContainsAddr(ip) {
		return h.txpool
	}
	return &NilPool{}
}
```

Ethhandler must be initialized using the `txGossipNetRestrict`.

We have these benefits
- We do not check peer ip every time for the inbound / outbound connection
    - Less likelihood to leak the txpool, since we check the filtering when txpool initialization. More easy to reason about the flow.
- Possibly less diff with upstream

fix(op-dispute-mon): prevent ignored games from retaining cached data

## Problem

**Description**

When a dispute game is added to the `ignoredGames` configuration, the monitor correctly increments the `ignored` counter and logs a warning, but **the game's previously cached data remains in the returned `enrichedGames` list**. This causes ignored games to still be processed by forecast and monitoring logic, creating a semantic inconsistency.

**Evidence**

1. **Test expectations**: The `IgnoreGames` test expects `len(enriched) == 1` when 2 games exist with 1 ignored
2. **Metric semantics**: `ignored_games` is documented as "games present in the game window but ignored via config"
3. **Actual behavior**: Ignored games with cached data still appear in results and are processed

## Tests

Added test case `IgnorePreviouslyCachedGame` that verifies:
1. A game is successfully enriched and cached
2. The game is added to ignoredGames
3. On next extraction, the game is not in results despite having cached data
4. The ignored counter is incremented correctly

**Description**

This PR adds two new optional configuration fields to the rollup config to make finality behavior configurable:

- finality_lookback: Controls the number of L1 blocks to look back for finality verification. When not set, uses the existing default calculation (129 blocks, or based on alt-DA challenge/resolve windows if alt-DA is enabled).
- finality_delay: Controls the number of L1 blocks to traverse before attempting to finalize L2 blocks again. When not set, defaults to 64 blocks.

**Tests**
No tests added in this PR. The changes follow the existing config pattern used by other optional fields (e.g., PectraBlobScheduleTime, AltDAConfig). The config validation is covered by the existing test infrastructure in types_test.go which validates JSON serialization/deserialization and round-tripping of config fields.

# docs(specs/experimental/contracts): create GovernanceToken specification

## Summary

Created a comprehensive specification for the GovernanceToken contract following the canonical format. The spec documents the ERC20 governance token with voting/delegation capabilities (ERC20Votes) and controlled minting through the MintManager owner. Key sections include:

- **Overview**: High-level description of the token's role in OP Stack governance
- **Assumptions**: Owner governance constraints and ERC20Votes supply limits
- **Invariants**: 3 invariants covering voting power accuracy, transfer freedom, and minting authorization
- **Function Specification**: Complete documentation of all public/external functions including mint, burn/burnFrom, delegation (delegate, delegateBySig), voting queries (getVotes, getPastVotes, etc.), and standard ERC20/ERC20Permit functions

The spec is based on the actual contract implementation at `packages/contracts-bedrock/src/governance/GovernanceToken.sol`, which is a straightforward composition of OpenZeppelin contracts (ERC20Burnable, ERC20Votes, Ownable) with a custom owner-only mint function.

**Note**: An experimental spec existed at `/specs/experimental/gov-token.md` describing GovernanceDelegation integration, but this was NOT implemented in the actual contract, so I based this spec on the simpler `/specs/governance/gov-token.md` and the actual contract code.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Verify inherited function behaviors are accurate**: The spec documents behavior from OpenZeppelin's ERC20Votes, ERC20Permit, and ERC20Burnable. Spot-check that documented behaviors (especially voting power updates, delegation mechanics, and signature validation) match the actual OpenZeppelin implementations used by the contract.

- [ ] **Review invariant classification**: Particularly iGT-003 ("Unauthorized minting is impossible") - confirm this is appropriate as an invariant rather than just being in the mint() function spec. The guidelines allow critical security properties in either location, but worth double-checking.

- [ ] **Validate assumptions are true external dependencies**: Especially aGT-002 about the ERC20Votes total supply constraint - is this really an "assumption" (external dependency) or just a technical limitation of the inherited implementation?

- [ ] **Confirm no experimental features were included**: The experimental spec at `/specs/experimental/gov-token.md` describes GovernanceDelegation hook integration that doesn't exist in the actual contract. Verify this spec correctly documents only what's actually implemented.

Created a new contract specification for the FaultDisputeGame family at `specs/experimental/contracts/dispute/fault-dispute-game.md`. This specification covers five contract variants that share the core bisection-based dispute resolution mechanism but differ in access control and architectural implementation:

- **FaultDisputeGame**: Base permissionless V1 implementation
- **PermissionedDisputeGame**: Permissioned V1 with proposer/challenger roles
- **SuperPermissionedDisputeGame**: Permissioned variant extending SuperFaultDisputeGame
- **FaultDisputeGameV2**: Permissionless V2 using Immutable Args Pattern
- **PermissionedDisputeGameV2**: Permissioned V2 with Immutable Args Pattern

The specification includes:
- Overview and Contract Variants sections explaining the family
- 9 Definitions (including Proposer Role, Challenger Role, Immutable Args Pattern)
- 3 Assumptions about external dependencies (AnchorStateRegistry, VM, DelayedWETH)
- 7 Invariants including new i01-007 for permissioned access control
- Complete function specifications for 30+ public/external functions

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Verify multi-variant approach**: Confirm that documenting all 5 variants in a single specification (rather than separate specs) aligns with documentation standards and makes sense for maintainability
- [ ] **Cross-check permission model**: Review invariant i01-007 and the permission-related updates to `initialize()`, `step()`, and `move()` functions against actual contract code to ensure accuracy, especially the distinction between which variants have which restrictions
- [ ] **Validate V2 architectural changes**: Check that the Immutable Args Pattern definition and V2-specific behaviors (especially in `initialize()` with variable calldata length) accurately reflect the architectural refactoring
- [ ] **Review invariants for completeness**: Verify that the 7 invariants capture all critical cross-function security properties, particularly around game resolution, bond distribution, and access control
- [ ] **Spot-check function behaviors**: Select 3-5 critical functions (e.g., `resolveClaim`, `closeGame`, `challengeRootL2Block`) and verify their MUST/MUST NOT requirements match actual contract implementation

### Notes

This specification was created entirely from code analysis without ability to test against actual deployments. The spec attempts to be comprehensive but may have missed subtle edge cases or variant-specific behaviors that aren't immediately obvious from code reading alone. Pay particular attention to areas where behavior differs between variants (especially V1 vs V2 and permissioned vs permissionless).

Add L2 Contract Management design doc

## Purpose

To enable deterministic, well tested, hard fork driven upgrades of L2 contracts, with both the implementation and upgrade path written in Solidity.

The customers for this work include:

- protocol devs seeking to modify L2 contracts
- chain operators looking for improvements
- anyone who has ever worried about unclear and inconsistent versioning of L2 contracts across OP chains

## Summary

The proposed design maintains the current method of injecting Network Upgrade Transactions (NUTs) at a specific fork block height, while improving on the development and testing process in order to better enable safe, well-tested, multi-client upgrades of L2 contracts.

This is achieved by putting the transaction data into a JSON file, and then executing it at the specified fork block.

The design aims to create a solution which parallels the OPCM, but for L2.

**Description**

Based on top of https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/17320

Enables OP Stack chains to use an asset other than ETH as their native fee currency by introducing a minimal, flexible, and standardizable Custom Gas Token (CGT) architecture. To do so, it introduces new **predeploys** (`NativeAssetLiquidity` and `LiquidityController`) that decouple native asset management from core bridging operations while using a single `isCustomGasToken()` flag that disables ETH transfer flows in all bridging methods. The two new pre-deploys manage the native asset supply.

# Add SuperFaultDisputeGame variant to FaultDisputeGame specification

## Summary

Added SuperFaultDisputeGame as the 6th variant to the FaultDisputeGame specification. SuperFaultDisputeGame is a permissionless variant designed for interoperability that validates super root claims using L2 sequence numbers (timestamps) instead of L2 block numbers. The specification now documents how SuperFaultDisputeGame differs from standard variants in initialization, data access, and state tracking.

**Key changes:**
- Updated Overview and Contract Variants sections to include SuperFaultDisputeGame (changed from 5 to 6 variants)
- Added two new definitions: "Super Root" (cross-chain state commitment) and "L2 Sequence Number" (timestamp-based identifier)
- Updated function specifications to document SuperFaultDisputeGame-specific behaviors:
  - `initialize`: Added validation rules for INVALID_ROOT_CLAIM constant and L2 chain ID must be zero
  - `l2SequenceNumber`: Documents timestamp behavior in SuperFaultDisputeGame vs block number in standard variants
  - `startingRootHash`: Documents use of startingProposal instead of startingOutputRoot
  - `addLocalData`: Documents DISPUTED_L2_BLOCK_NUMBER loading l2SequenceNumber
- Added `startingSequenceNumber` function spec (only exists in SuperFaultDisputeGame variants)

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Verify SuperFaultDisputeGame description accuracy**: Cross-check the variant description against actual SuperFaultDisputeGame.sol contract and interop design docs to ensure the purpose and key differences are accurately captured
- [ ] **Validate function specifications**: Review all updated function specs (initialize, l2SequenceNumber, startingRootHash, startingSequenceNumber, addLocalData) against SuperFaultDisputeGame.sol source code to verify technical accuracy
- [ ] **Check for completeness**: Verify no other SuperFaultDisputeGame-specific functions or behaviors are missing from the spec (e.g., are there other functions that behave differently in SuperFaultDisputeGame?)
- [ ] **Verify technical details**: Confirm offset values (88 for l2SequenceNumber), constant names (INVALID_ROOT_CLAIM), validation rules (L2 chain ID must be zero), and data structure references (startingProposal vs startingOutputRoot) are correct

### Notes

This specification was created by analyzing the SuperFaultDisputeGame.sol contract code. The definitions for "Super Root" and "L2 Sequence Number" are based on code comments and behavior, so they should be reviewed by someone familiar with the interop design to ensure they accurately reflect the intended interop concepts.

# Link defined terms to their definitions throughout contract specs

## Summary

Added markdown links for all defined terms throughout the contract specification documents in `specs/experimental/contracts/`. When a term is defined in a document's "Definitions" section, all occurrences of that term throughout the document are now linked to the definition using markdown syntax `[Term Name](#anchor-link)`.

**Files modified**: 20 markdown files across L1, L2, cannon, dispute, safe, and universal directories

**Examples of changes**:
- "authorized portal" → "[Authorized Portal](#authorized-portal)"
- "message hash" → "[Message Hash](#message-hash)"  
- "admin" → "[Admin](#admin)"
- Plural forms handled correctly: "authorized portals" → "[Authorized Portals](#authorized-portal)"

**Implementation approach**: Used Python scripts to systematically process each file, identifying defined terms and linking occurrences while avoiding code blocks, the Definitions section itself, and the auto-generated TOC. Line lengths were automatically wrapped to comply with markdown linting rules, and TOCs were regenerated to reflect the changes.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

**Risk level**: 🟡 Yellow (automated changes across many files with limited testing)

- [ ] **Spot-check link correctness**: Open 3-4 modified files and click several term links to verify they navigate to the correct definition anchor
- [ ] **Verify no over-linking**: Check that terms inside backticks (like `_admin` parameters), code blocks, and function names were NOT linked
- [ ] **Check line wrapping**: Review files with many wrapped lines (proxy.md, fault-dispute-game.md, preimage-oracle.md) to ensure readability wasn't compromised
- [ ] **Test rendered docs**: Run `just serve` locally and navigate through several spec files to verify the links work in the rendered documentation

### Test Plan
```bash

cd ~/repos/specs
just serve
```

### Notes
- The automated approach means if there's a bug in the link logic, it could be replicated across multiple files - thorough spot-checking is important
